SYNTHETIC TEST DOCUMENT - FICTIONAL PATIENT - NOT FOR CLINICAL USE
ERCP REPORT
Facility: Oakhurst Regional Medical Center (fictional)
Patient: Ambrose Whitcombe (fictional)
Date of service: November 4, 2026
Endoscopist: Farida Kessler-Moore, MD (fictional)
Indication: Choledocholithiasis on MRCP with abnormal liver tests.
Procedure: The duodenoscope was advanced to the major papilla, which appeared normal.
Deep biliary cannulation was achieved with a sphincterotome and a guidewire.
Cholangiogram: the bile duct was dilated to 12 mm with three filling defects (stones).
A biliary sphincterotomy was performed with blended current, without bleeding.
Three stones, the largest 9 mm, were extracted from the bile duct with an extraction balloon.
An occlusion cholangiogram showed no residual filling defects.
Fluoroscopy images were interpreted separately by the radiology service.
Impression: Choledocholithiasis; biliary sphincterotomy and complete balloon stone extraction.
Plan: Observe overnight for post-ERCP pancreatitis.
